findings.section: Decided here / How a report is compared with its golden
findings.summary: The cut rule does not identify the session table uniquely, and the Go-side end marker cannot be parsed. Python's `plan` and `gate-review` reports have a second table whose heading also starts `| round |`: the kept gate verdicts, which the brief says stay byte for byte. The Go Sessions block has blank lines inside it (after the heading, after the fence, before `Permission denials:`), and a report holds one block per brief, so 'from `Sessions (` through the blank line before the next section' does not say where the block ends.
findings.evidence: tools/copilot-acceptance/report.py:205 `| round | record | ...` (the session table) and :226 `| round | verdict | gate-verdict/v2 | findings by kind |`. report.py:271 `| round | verdict | gate-verdict/v2 |` in plan_report. P2's block layout: heading, blank line, fence, blank line, `Session records:`, record lines, `Permission denials:`, blank line, denial lines.
findings.fix: Cut only the first table of the Python output: from its heading line through the blank line after it. Build the expected Go output from the golden with that table replaced by the Sessions block(s) the test composes: the fenced `vloop metrics <run id> --by session` stdout plus the literal record and denial lines. Then compare the whole Go output with it byte for byte. That removes the need for any Go-side end marker.

findings.section: Decided here (@DIR@) / P3 / Worked example P3
findings.summary: @DIR@ is defined only for outputs. The P3 inputs need the temp dir too, and resolved and unresolved forms will be mixed. The fixture `copilot-argv.log` gives the session's `cwd` (subprocess.run runs there, so it must exist) and `env COPILOT_HOME` (hook.py writes hooks/vloop-fence.json into it). Both must point into the test's temp dir, so the fixture has to be templated. Python joins `d` as given (`<d>/shims`, `<d>/bin/vloop`), but a stub that records `pwd -P` sees the resolved path (`/private/var/...` on macOS). The two forms then appear in one golden, and replacing a single form leaves the other.
findings.evidence: report.py:66-79 and hook.py:43-53: cwd and env come from the log, and PATH is prefixed with os.path.join(d, "shims"). hook.py:61 builds `--root '<cwd>'` and `'<d>/bin/vloop'`. hook.py:74-76 writes to `$COPILOT_HOME/hooks/`. run.sh's wrapper logs `cwd $(pwd -P)`. hook.py:59 also reads VLOOP_HOOK_PHASE from the process environment.
findings.fix: State this: fixture files hold @DIR@ where the temp dir goes, and the test (and the golden generator) substitute the temp dir resolved with EvalSymlinks / `pwd -P` when they copy them. The same resolved dir is passed as `<dir>` to both programs. Only that form is replaced back by @DIR@ in outputs. VLOOP_HOOK_PHASE is unset (or pinned) in both runs.

findings.section: Shape task 5 gate / P4 README / Constraints (goldens)
findings.summary: Task 5's gate fails any file under tools/copilot-acceptance/ outside kit/testdata/ that mentions `python3`, `report.py` or `hook.py`. Three things the brief asks for or leaves open can trip it. P4 has the README say the kit needs go, copilot and gh, 'not python3'. Task 2's gate needs a golden generator that runs python3 on report.py/hook.py, and the brief does not say where it lives: if it is a Go test or file under kit/ it trips the grep and also breaks 'No go test needs python3'. And the kit's Go source naturally documents itself as the port of report.py.
findings.evidence: Shape 5: 'a check that no file under tools/copilot-acceptance/ outside kit/testdata/ mentions python3, report.py or hook.py'. P4: 'README.md says the kit needs go, copilot and gh … not python3'. Constraints: 'Task 2's gate takes both from the base … regenerates the goldens there'. The generator's location is not named anywhere.
findings.fix: Pin the generator to kit/testdata/ (for example `tools/copilot-acceptance/kit/testdata/gen.sh <python dir> <vloop> <out dir>`, a shell script that no go test runs). Task 2 writes it and task 2's gate runs it. Say the README names no Python at all (it lists what the kit needs) and that the kit's Go source does not name the deleted files, or narrow the grep to the scripts and the README.

findings.section: Worked example P1 / Behaviour contract P1 Text (turns)
findings.summary: The fixture 'a legacy shell-loop record (total_cost_usd, no turns) → turns -' does not describe real legacy records. Every shell-loop record carries `num_turns`, which vloop's own driver reads as turns. Under 'turns, - when absent' (reading `turns`), every legacy row in this repository shows `-` although the record has the count, and the brief never says this is intended.
findings.evidence: .loop/state/runs/B20260929-1804-vloop-skeleton-config-briefs/20260929-194129/sessions/001-work.json has keys incl. num_turns, total_cost_usd, modelUsage and no turns. internal/driver/agent.go:185 `get("num_turns", &turns)`. internal/runs/runs.go:410-435 (rawSession) reads neither field today.
findings.fix: Decide it explicitly. My recommendation: `turns` is the record's `turns`, else `num_turns`. Change the fixture to a legacy record with num_turns 7 → turns 7, and keep a 'no turns at all' case if wanted. Or state that legacy rows show `-` deliberately.

findings.summary: `report.py second` lists run.log lines and dissents in `glob.glob` order, unsorted (directory order, filesystem-dependent). With more than one run folder in its fixture, the golden's order is arbitrary, and the Go program cannot reproduce it byte for byte, or does so only by luck.
findings.evidence: tools/copilot-acceptance/report.py:131 and :134: `glob.glob(...run.log) + glob.glob(...)` and the same for iterations.jsonl, with no sorted().
findings.fix: Say the `second` fixture has exactly one run.log and one iterations.jsonl (or that the Go program sorts and the fixture has one folder, so both orders agree).

findings.summary: P2 does not say what replaces the session table when no run id qualifies (no `.vloop/state/runs/<id>/`, or no matching brief file), for example a run that halted before creating its folder. Python prints the empty table, and the Go program would print nothing in its place or something unpinned.
findings.evidence: P2: 'for each <run id> whose <repo>/.vloop/state/runs/<run id>/ directory exists and whose docs/briefs/<run id>.loop-brief.md exists … one block per brief'. No zero-brief case. report.py prints the header rows regardless.
findings.fix: Pin a literal, for example `Sessions: no brief with runs.`, and add a worked-example line (report run on a repository with no runs → that line, the rest as the golden).

decisions: --by session as a --by value, not a new `vloop sessions` command: agree.

by_session as an optional property of metrics/v4, no v5; export deletes it as it deletes by_task, and --workspace --json carries it: agree (schema has no additionalProperties: false, export.go:190 already deletes by_task).
The kit as one Go package main run with `go -C "$top" run`, not a vloop subcommand, no jq: agree.
Byte-for-byte reproduction of the Python, frozen as goldens produced by the base's Python (git show <base>:…) and regenerated by task 2's gate: agree, given findings 1-3.

The reports' per-kind filtered session tables (work-only, verify-only, session/v4-only for second, gate-review rounds) are replaced by every session of the brief, and schema checks use each record's own schema instead of a fixed session/v3 or v4. This changes what b24/b25/b26/b27/c5 summaries show from now on: agree, but the operator should know the round column of gate-review is gone.
When `vloop metrics` fails, the report goes on with an error line: agree.
Denial text precedence message > command > file_path > tool_input.command > tool_input.file_path: agree; it covers every shape in this repository's records.
`#` three digits, credits `-` vs `0.00`, second-review rows phase `second-review`: agree.
Legacy rows' turns: undecided in the brief, see finding 4; I recommend reading num_turns.
